newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan tells Iran its planes did not raid Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Sudan tells Iran its planes did not raid Uganda.

text.p: Sudan has told Iran that Sudanese planes did not bomb northern Uganda but did attack southern Sudanese rebels inside Sudan.

Iran's embassy in Nairobi said on Tuesday the denial was given by Sudanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Mustafa Osman Ismail by telephone on Monday to Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Sheikhul Islam.
"Sudan will refute whatever has been published by some news agencies that Sudanese aircraft attacked Ugandan territory," Ismail was quoted by the Iranian embassy statement as saying.

Under a September 9 pact mediated by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, Sudan and Uganda agreed to work to halt rebel activity in the border area. They accuse each other of supporting rebel groups.

The Iranian statement quoted Ismail as saying "some rebels in southern Sudan were initiating a military attack against Sudan, therefore Sudanese aircraft attacked their own territory within eight miles (13 km) of the Sudanese boundaries".
It said Ismail added "if it is proved that aircraft mistakenly raided Ugandan territory, his country will officially apologise to the government of Uganda".
He said under the agreement between Sudan and Uganda mediated by Iran, Khartoum was ready to send a high-level mission to Iran to take part in a tripartite meeting.
The Sudanese armed forces denied on Monday its warplanes bombed northern Uganda on Sunday and said such claims harmed the agreement to normalise relations.
"This news -- if really stated by the Ugandan state minister of defence -- is untrue," the official Sudan News Agency quoted General Mohammed el-Sanousi, spokesman of the armed forces, as saying.

Uganda's Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi had said two Sudanese MiG planes on Sunday dropped bombs aimed at an army barracks in the northwestern town of Moyo, 16 km (10 miles) south of Sudan's border, but missed their target.
"It is true we have been bombed by Sudan...It is surprising that even before the ink dries on the agreement we signed they are bombing us," Mbabazi told reporters.
"We shall not sit back and watch while our territory continues to be violated. We shall soon respond appropriately."
An aid worker, who declined to be named, said: "Two Sudanese MiGs came over on Sunday and dropped a number of bombs, around 10. Not all fell on Moyo and we have no reports of casualties,"
